original: The development of precision instrumentation in laboratories transformed how scholars understood natural phenomena during the early modern period. Microscopy and telescope design enabled observation at scales previously inaccessible to the human eye. It seems reasonable to conclude that such technical innovations fundamentally altered the epistemic foundations of empirical inquiry. Standardization of measurement protocols gradually emerged as these instruments became more refined and widely adopted. The resulting capacity for replicable observation arguably constitutes one of the central achievements of this transformation in scientific method.
